purpose: liblhasa is a library for reading/decompressing LHA archives.

functions.lha_input_stream_new: Creates an `LHAInputStream` wrapper around a caller-provided `handle` and stream `type`. Use it to initialize a new input stream object; it sets lead-in length to 0 and state to `LHA_INPUT_STREAM_INIT`. Returns `NULL` on allocation failure.
functions.lha_reader_free: Frees an `LHAReader` and all owned resources. Call it when done reading. It closes any active decoder, frees all stacked directory/file headers, frees the underlying basic reader, then frees `reader` itself.
functions.lha_input_stream_free:
`lha_input_stream_free` closes an `LHAInputStream` if its type provides a `close` callback, then frees the stream object itself. Use it when you’re done with a stream. If `close` is `NULL`, only the wrapper is freed.
Only pass a valid, fully initialized LHAInputStream created by supported constructors such as lha_input_stream_from() or lha_input_stream_from_FILE(). Do not call lha_input_stream_free() on an object returned from lha_input_stream_new(NULL, NULL) or any stream whose type field may be NULL. Ensure constructor arguments are non-NULL and call free only when stream != NULL and initialization succeeded.
functions.lha_reader_extract: `lha_reader_extract` extracts the current entry from `reader`. Use it after positioning on a file; pass an output `filename` (or `NULL` for fake dirs to use the entry path) and optional progress callback. Returns 1 on success, 0 if at START/EOF or unsupported state.
functions.lha_reader_check: `lha_reader_check` verifies the current entry’s integrity by decoding it and checking CRC. Use it only when `curr_file_type == CURR_FILE_NORMAL`; directories return 1 immediately. If the entry isn’t normal, it returns 0.
functions.lha_decoder_monitor: Registers a progress callback for `LHADecoder`. Call it before/while decoding to receive progress updates via `callback_data`. It scales `block_size` up for very large streams so reported blocks stay ≤128K and avoid 32-bit overflow, then triggers an initial progress check.
functions.lha_reader_new: Creates a new `LHAReader` for reading an LHA archive from an `LHAInputStream`. Use it with a valid stream; it allocates the reader and initializes state. Returns `NULL` on allocation failure or if the underlying basic reader can’t be created.
functions.lha_decoder_free: `lha_decoder_free` destroys an `LHADecoder`. Use it on a decoder created by the library. If the decoder type has a `free` callback, it frees decoder-specific data at `decoder+1`, then frees the decoder itself.
functions.lha_decoder_get_crc: Returns the decoder’s current CRC value. Use it after/while decoding to inspect checksum state for the archive entry. It simply reads `decoder->crc`; no side effects, validation, or special-case handling.
functions.lha_reader_read: `lha_reader_read` reads decompressed bytes from the current file. Call it after selecting/opening an entry; on first use it lazily creates the decoder. It returns bytes read, or `0` if decoder setup fails or no more data is available.
functions.lha_reader_current_is_fake: Returns nonzero if the current entry is a synthetic one: a fake directory or deferred symlink. Use it after selecting/reading the current item to detect entries that aren’t real stored files. Otherwise returns 0.
functions.lha_decoder_new64: Creates a new decoder object for a given `dtype`, callback, and input stream length. It allocates one zeroed block for the decoder, private state, and output buffer. Returns `NULL` on allocation failure; otherwise initializes fields like `stream_pos`, `stream_length`, and CRC.
functions.lha_input_stream_from: Creates an `LHAInputStream` from a file path. It opens `filename` in binary read mode, wraps the `FILE*` in a stream, and returns `NULL` if `fopen` fails or stream creation fails. On failure after open, it closes the file.
functions.lha_decoder_for_name: Looks up an LHA decoder type by its name string. Pass a decoder name matching `decoders[i].name`; it returns that `LHADecoderType*`. If no match is found, it returns `NULL`.
functions.lha_decoder_read: `lha_decoder_read` copies up to `buf_len` decompressed bytes into `buf`. It’s meant for incremental reads from an `LHADecoder`. It truncates at `stream_length` to avoid extra bytes at EOF, and may return fewer bytes than requested when data runs out.
functions.lha_decoder_get_length64: `lha_decoder_get_length64()` returns the decoder’s current stream position as a 64-bit length (`decoder->stream_pos`). Use it after/while decoding to query how many bytes have been processed. It just returns the stored value; no extra checks or side effects.
functions.lha_reader_next_file: Advances the reader to the next LHA entry, cleaning up any active decoder first. Use it to iterate files sequentially. Returns `NULL` at EOF; if the previous entry was a fake dir, it is freed before moving on.
functions.lha_reader_set_dir_policy: Sets the reader’s directory-handling policy. Call it on an initialized `LHAReader` before reading entries to choose how directories are treated during extraction/iteration. It just stores the enum value; no validation or other side effects.
functions.lha_input_stream_from_FILE: Creates an `LHAInputStream` that reads from an existing `FILE*` without taking ownership. It first sets the stream to binary mode, then wraps it for liblhasa input. Use it with a valid open `FILE*`; the caller remains responsible for closing it.
